solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Translation of Camus volumes taking year — and know-how

indicators.note: a translation renders a text into another form, so the name is rewritten in a new order

blocks.note: the French writer's name, taken as written
V is the abbreviation for volume, doubled for the plural
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A translator works on several volumes of Camus over a year and brings expertise to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' simply adds the year after the volumes. CUMSAVVY is a Chambers word, spelt as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Savvy, and the jokey variant cumsavvy, mean practical shrewdness or understanding, which is what know-how names.

clue.text: Peak abandoned by men with feeble strength? Excusable fault (10, two words)

indicators.note: when something is abandoned by a group, that group leaves it, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: culmen is the Latin-derived word for a summit or top
taken as written, and removed
pale can mean weak or feeble, as in a pale imitation
vis is force or power, from Latin

explanation.surface: A mountain summit is given up by climbers too weak to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the feeble word to the strength word. The phrase is Latin legal terminology.
explanation.definitionFit: Culpa levis is the law term for slight negligence, a minor blameworthy failing that can be pardoned.

clue.text: After universal might, time's up for caliph

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
may and might are both forms of the same auxiliary verb, and may also means power
a day is a time, as in 'in my day'

explanation.surface: After a period of universal power, the end has come for a Muslim ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just orders the pieces: the universal and might letters come first, then the reversed time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Umayyads were a dynasty of caliphs ruling from Damascus, so any one of them is an example of a caliph.

clue.text: Aromatic fruit from Middle East in part of summer?

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: ME is the standard abbreviation for Middle East
a month at the start of the warm season

explanation.surface: A fragrant fruit imported from the Middle East during the summer months.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamey is a tropical American tree whose large fruit is fragrant and sweet-fleshed.

clue.text: Robed in chasuble that's hired out (not by owner)

indicators.note: a body robed in a garment is wrapped inside it, so the letters sit inside these words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the vestment word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone in a priest's vestment that is rented rather than owned.
explanation.walkthrough: A chasuble is the sleeveless vestment a priest wears to celebrate Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: To sublet is to let property one is renting oneself, so the letting is done by a tenant rather than the owner.

clue.text: Fermentation vessel that's got in for a yield of grapes

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it into that other's place

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank used for fermenting wine or beer
taken as written
taken as written: the letter to be swapped out

explanation.surface: A wine vat that has been filled with a harvest of grapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vint is an old word for a vintage, the crop of grapes gathered in one season.

clue.text: Fly landed on one — cross about that

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it on both sides

blocks.note: lit is a past tense of light, to come down and settle
a means one, as in 'a dozen'
to put a cross on a ballot paper is to vote

explanation.surface: An insect settles on someone, who is annoyed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as the insect, but it is the verb defined; 'cross' is not angry but the mark on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Volitate is a rare verb meaning to flutter or fly, from the Latin for to fly about.

clue.text: Lake fish, 100 known

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
in the biblical sense, to have known someone is to have had them

explanation.surface: An angler's report of a lake where a hundred fish are known to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and a charade all lead to the same four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Chad is a large lake in central Africa, and chad is also a name for a young sea bream.

clue.text: Well-known monogram made by husband in what denotes hand

indicators.note: something put in a word is set inside its letters

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
chiro- is the word-forming element meaning hand, as in chiropody

explanation.surface: A husband's initials inked into the hand as a famous emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The chi-rho is the familiar Christian monogram made from the first two Greek letters of Christ's name.

clue.text: Die loaded, as old scamp who's lost his way

indicators.note: someone who has lost something no longer has it, so those letters go

blocks.note: a highwayman was a mounted robber of old
taken as written, and removed

explanation.surface: A rogue of the past gambles with loaded dice, having wandered off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost his way' sounds like going astray; here the word way is literally taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A high man was a crooked die weighted to throw high numbers, in old gamblers' slang.

clue.text: Animated greeting welcomes brave hero on leaving

indicators.note: the word on leaving means those two letters depart from the word before
a host who welcomes a guest takes them inside

blocks.note: a lion is the type of courage, and a brave person is lion-hearted
taken as written, and removed
ave is the Latin word of greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A lively welcome is given to a courageous champion as he departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive can mean lively or full of energy, which is what animated describes.

clue.text: Recording enthusiast, I twice help a duo struggling

indicators.note: things struggling thrash about out of place, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letter I, given two times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hi-fi lover asks two times for help from a pair of performers in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiophile is a devotee of high-quality sound reproduction, someone keen on recordings.

clue.text: Innocents — those first in line are making baa-ing sounds

indicators.note: the first ones in a line are the leading members, so only initial letters count

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Guileless creatures at the front of a queue are bleating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures sheep, and the initials do spell the young of the sheep, a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is a standard figure of meekness and guiltlessness, so innocent people are called lambs.

clue.text: Sponge is required to reverse Magic Marker?

indicators.note: reversing runs a thing backwards, so the letters read from the end

blocks.note: to lig is British slang for to freeload or sponge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone needs a sponge to wipe away a felt-tip pen's marks.
explanation.walkthrough: Magic Marker is a brand of felt-tip pen, but here it means a mark used in magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigil is a seal or occult sign believed to have magical power, so it is a mark that works magic.

clue.text: One of the hellebores, note, among Noel trees growing wild (10, two words)

indicators.note: something among others is mixed in with them
plants growing wild sprawl without order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for note
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on a hellebore found among Christmas trees running riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel is Christmas, and the Christmas rose is another hellebore, a tempting wrong turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lenten rose, Helleborus orientalis, is a hellebore that flowers in late winter and early spring.

clue.text: Confusion: drunk is exhibiting renal problem

blocks.note: pye is a variant of pie, printers' jumbled type, hence confusion
lit is slang for intoxicated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled drinker shows signs of kidney trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusion' and 'drunk' look like anagram signals but each gives its own word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyelitis is inflammation of the pelvis of the kidney, a disorder of the renal system.

clue.text: Media advertisers exploiting chimp with net

indicators.note: exploiting something means working it for use, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ad men making use of an ape and a net in their campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchmen are salespeople who make the sales pitch, such as presenters of advertisements on television or radio.

clue.text: Seclude, last of sun having gone in? Certainly not

definitions.text: Seclude, last of sun having gone in? Certainly not

indicators.note: a thing that has gone in something is now inside it
'last of' keeps only the last letter of 'sun'

blocks.note: to isolate is to set apart
the final letter of sun

explanation.surface: Should one shut oneself away once the sun has set? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: it builds a word for 'seclude' with the sun's letter inside, then says the meaning is the opposite, putting someone out in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To insolate is to expose to the sun's rays, the reverse of keeping someone hidden away indoors.

clue.text: This plant an American has inside?

indicators.note: what a phrase has inside is contained within its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Is this a shrub that grows in American homes?
explanation.walkthrough: The word plant does double duty, as part of the definition and as the start of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a genus of tropical American shrubs of the verbena family, grown for their flower clusters.

clue.text: Painkiller, one for unfortunates laid up? It's swallowed

indicators.note: something swallowed is taken inside, so the letters lie within the phrase
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A tablet for the poor souls who are bedridden, taken by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' suggests being ill in bed, which suits a painkiller, but in a down clue it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurofen is a brand of ibuprofen tablets, widely sold in Britain to relieve pain.

clue.text: Drink to a sot is drunk before or after 'Time'

indicators.note: something drunk is tipsy and unsteady, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunkard downs a glass just before or after the landlord calls time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before or after' is literal: the time letter can go first or last, since the jumble can also give TOAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to raise a glass and drink in their honour.

clue.text: Freshwater fish seen from below is ghastly

indicators.note: in a down clue, viewing from below reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
lurid can mean gruesome or horrifying

explanation.surface: A river fish looks hideous when viewed from underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A silurid is a member of the Siluridae, a family of freshwater catfish.

clue.text: Develop low throw, switching front pair

indicators.note: switching the front pair swaps the two leading letters, a small rearrangement

blocks.note: a deuce is a two at dice, the lowest throw after the ace

explanation.surface: Instructions for improving a weak bowling delivery by changing the leading two players.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or bring forth something latent, which is to develop it.

clue.text: Head of state giving his country (briefly) a sort out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba
taken as written

explanation.surface: A national leader gives his nation a thorough overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' points to the answer's own country, Cuba, reduced to its single-letter vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro was Cuba's long-serving leader, president of the country until 2008.

clue.text: This wee sparkler wi' 5th of November is streamin' flickeringly

indicators.note: a flickering light jumps about unsteadily, so the letters are jumbled
the answer with an added letter forms the jumbled word, so that letter must come off again

blocks.note: taken as written, the dropped final g shown by the apostrophe
the fifth letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: In Scots dialect, a little firework on Bonfire Night streams and flickers.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus the extra letter rearranges to the given word. The 5th of November is Bonfire Night, when Britain sets off fireworks such as sparklers.
explanation.definitionFit: Starnie is a Scots diminutive of starn, meaning a little star, something small that twinkles.

clue.text: River willow and flowering bush looking more promising

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
an osier is a willow used in basketwork

explanation.surface: A riverside willow and a blossoming shrub look healthier than before.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay and two definitions all give the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosier is an old word for a rose bush, and as the comparative of rosy it means more hopeful.

clue.text: Navigational aid used before progress in ebbing ocean gulfs

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the letters run backwards
a thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: VOR, VHF omnidirectional range, is a radio beacon system for aircraft navigation
an ocean is a sea
to go is to proceed or make headway

explanation.surface: A navigation beacon helps ships move forward through the receding tides into deep bays.
explanation.definitionFit: A voragoes, plural of vorago, is a chasm or abyss, so the word names deep gulfs.

clue.text: Monk without tan, one with sallow complexion?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: the Olivetans are a Benedictine order of monks
taken as written, and removed

explanation.surface: A pallid monk with no suntan looks sickly yellowish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tan' seems to belong with complexion, but it is the letters to strike from the monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive describes a yellowish-brown skin tone, so a person so described has a sallow complexion.

clue.text: Front of bonnet in foreign car showing inverted V?

indicators.note: a letter placed in a word sits inside its letters
'Front of' keeps only the first letter of 'bonnet'

blocks.note: the opening letter of bonnet
Lada is a Russian make of car

explanation.surface: The front of a foreign car's bonnet has an upside-down V badge.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonnet is the British name for a car's hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Labda is an old spelling of lambda, the Greek letter whose capital looks like a V turned upside down.

clue.text: Prehistoric monster: complete bone found by university in Arabia

indicators.note: something placed in a word is put inside it

blocks.note: all means whole or complete
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone
U is the abbreviation for university
Ar is a dictionary abbreviation for Arabic or Arabia

explanation.surface: A complete dinosaur skeleton is unearthed by a university dig in Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: The allosaur was a large carnivorous dinosaur of the Jurassic, a monster from prehistory.

clue.text: Towering projection in part of the Mesozoic era

indicators.note: towering means rising upward, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: a sail is a projecting arm of a windmill

explanation.surface: A high-rising outcrop of rock dates from the age of dinosaurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lias is the lowest division of the Jurassic, one of the periods making up the Mesozoic.

clue.text: Riddles fit to be worked out on board?

indicators.note: something worked out is reshaped, so its letters are reordered
being on a ship means being aboard it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: SS, steamship, is the usual stand-in for a ship to be on board
taken as written

explanation.surface: Puzzles suitable to be solved on a board or during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddles' looks like puzzles but is the verb for sieving.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to pass through a coarse sieve, so riddles and sifts are the same action.

clue.text: Prefabricated board building in a circle though knocked over

indicators.note: a thing knocked over lies the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an orb is a sphere or circle
if can mean even though, as in 'pleasant if dull'

explanation.surface: A prefab house built in a ring, even though it fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: Fibro is chiefly Australian usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibro is fibro-cement sheeting, and in Australia a fibro is a house built from these boards.

clue.text: Energy-filled Toad v Rest, wacky — like his passions?

indicators.note: something filled has another thing put inside it
wacky means crazy and disordered, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
taken as written, the v standing as a letter

explanation.surface: An energetic Toad takes on everyone else in a madcap contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is famous for wild enthusiasms, such as his craze for motor cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad's crazes were exaggerated and over the top, so his passions could be described as overstated.

clue.text: Stoic's teacher offering branch of religion, old

blocks.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A philosopher's mentor teaches an ancient school of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium founded Stoicism and taught in Athens, so he was the original teacher of the Stoics.

clue.text: Plodding inspector in case read mistakenly

indicators.note: something done mistakenly is wrongly arranged, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull police inspector misreads the evidence in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' suggests a police case, but it is a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lestrade is the unimaginative Scotland Yard detective whom Sherlock Holmes repeatedly outshines.
